Needs changes before merge.

This is a safety-tier review. The PR includes the post changes from #2342. Those changes affect posted G-code.

The guide clearly limits the example to an air cut. It identifies the end-face cut and the limits of stock simulation. The project, tables, excerpts, pictures, and links have useful tests.

Local results:

- The trial merge with upstream/main `7903db4dc82e299436d415096865c8f37291a2c9` is clean.
- The selected app test targets build. Eight suites pass: first_4axis_part (4), fourth_axis_pose (9), index_swing (13), recorded_post_streams (5), rotary_feed_cap (11), tormach_fourth_axis (12), tormach_post (10), and tormach_wrapped_a (10).
- continuous_4axis_part: 4 pass and 1 fails. microarc_test_part: 1 passes and 1 fails. Both failures compare posted NC text.
- The post suites pass: explain_tormach (3), recorded_streams (12), and script_tormach (11).
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- All 13 new site tests pass. Full site discovery reports three assertion failures and three errors. I reproduced the three assertion failures on unchanged upstream main. The three errors occur because Zola is not installed. `zola check` could not run.
- The quick gate dry run completed. Its broad plan includes shared goldens and changes from main. I ran the affected suites above, not the full gate.

Requested before merge:

1. **[P1] Resolve the inherited feed-time defect before this stack merges.** `assets/posts/tormach.cps:875` uses endpoint distance to calculate feed time. That distance does not bound the curved part-relative trajectory during a turning move. I reproduced the finding from #2342 on this trial merge. A rapid reaches world `(0, 0, 10)` at A0. A feed then holds that world point, turns to A3, and requests F0.1 mm/min. The post reports no warning and writes:

   ```text
   G93 G1 X0 Y0.523 Z9.986 A3 F57.735
   ```

   I sampled the posted XYZ/A interpolation at 10,000 intervals and transformed each point into the part frame. The path measures 0.006861819340 mm. Its average feed is 0.396167139577 mm/min, almost four times the requested feed. Bound the actual trajectory when calculating time, or refuse the move. Add an independent trajectory test. The fix belongs in #2342; refresh and test this child after that fix.

2. **[P2] Make both NC comparisons pass on supported platforms.** `crates/app/tests/continuous_4axis_part.rs:310` fails on Linux. The loaded project posts 3,213 lines, but nine differ from the committed program. At line 41, Linux writes `A43.171`; the example has `A43.172`. At lines 770-771, Linux writes `A46.549 F232.558` and `A45 F232.408`. The example has `A46.548 F232.408` and `A45 F232.558`. Other differences occur at lines 870-871, 2268-2269, and 3188-3189. The inherited comparison at `crates/app/tests/microarc_test_part.rs:265` also fails on nine lines, as reported on #2342. Use deterministic rounding or a narrowly bounded numeric comparison. Keep the independent rate checks. Replacing a golden with output from one platform does not establish a fix across platforms.

   ```text
   continuous_4axis_part: FAILED. 4 passed; 1 failed
   the_committed_project_posts_the_committed_program
   microarc_test_part: FAILED. 1 passed; 1 failed
   a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a
   ```

3. **[P3] Keep #1904 open for the missing acceptance evidence.** The PR body uses `Fixes #1904`. However, `docs/decisions/1904-continuous-4axis-walkthrough.md:55` confirms that no complete Hub run was done. The issue requires both programs to run to M30, with the results recorded there. It also requests a wrapped engraving or slot. The guide states that this operation is unavailable. Change the closing keyword to `Refs #1904` for this partial delivery. Alternatively, complete and record the remaining acceptance work before using `Fixes`.

Mutation checks:

- I changed the CPS text in memory through a temporary test harness outside the repository. Repository code stayed unchanged.
- Remove the A-rate time bound: RED. The rate test emits F598.962 instead of F4.
- Remove angle unwrapping: RED. The cumulative-A test emits A-179 instead of A181.
- Disable both mutations: GREEN. All 10 original wrapped-A tests pass.
- The separate trajectory/feed test remains RED on the unmodified post, as described in finding 1.

Golden checks:

- I compared every line of each generated NC program with its committed file. Each program has nine differing lines, as described above.
- I checked every NC line in both committed programs and both Linux outputs for feed mode, positive F, A travel, A continuity within a section, A rate, and G94 before rapids and section ends. These checks pass.
- I sampled each turning feed at 64 intervals. Neither example exceeds 8.001 in/min in that check. This does not clear the separate low-feed failure.
- The changed tilt refusal matches the recorded-stream test.

No PR change affects crates/ui. Before/after UI screenshots are not required. No restricted build script, workflow, scripts/ file, or dependency changes are present. No GitHub runner was used. No hardware or Hub run was done.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed:

1. P1: Merged parent #2342 at `b93fe06131248f91e41e90104e0d050409add852`. Feed time now bounds the rounded, curved part-relative trajectory. Refreshed the continuous example program and guide explanation. Pin: `posted_trajectory_length_obeys_the_feed_even_for_coincident_world_endpoints`. The old endpoint law is RED in metric and inch units; restoring the bound is GREEN. The continuous loaded-project test also samples the generated trajectory independently.

2. P2: Both NC comparisons now allow narrowly bounded platform rounding. XYZ, modes and structure remain exact. Pins: `permits_one_a_rounding_step_and_its_exact_rate_limited_feed`, `wrap_golden_allows_only_bounded_platform_rounding`, and their rejection checks. Strict comparison makes both synthetic platform-pair pins RED; restoration is GREEN. Wider allowances also fail the rejection pins. Both actual programs compare byte-identically on Linux after the intentional safety-law refresh. Independent feed and A-rate checks remain and pass.

3. P3: Changed the PR body to `Refs #1904`. It states the missing Hub runs to M30 and wrapped engraving or slot. The PR-body check is GREEN; replacing Refs with Fixes makes it RED. No Hub or hardware run is claimed.

Validation: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 589 steps. App/post clippy passed with all targets and `-D warnings`. All 13 affected site tests passed. Independent trajectory audits of both programs passed the programmed feed and 360 deg/min A limit.

New head: `764df9f4ebf32b22a550bc816d9fd86a67cc42aa`.

Please re-review. The PR remains a draft. Existing labels are unchanged.

Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is a safety-tier review. The PR includes the post changes from #2342. These changes affect posted G-code.

The three earlier findings are met:

1. The post bounds the curved trajectory from the rounded XYZ and A words. The independent trajectory test passes in metric and inch units.
2. Both NC comparisons pass locally. The numeric allowances are bounded. The tests retain exact XYZ, mode and structure checks. The independent rate checks pass.
3. The PR body uses `Refs #1904`. It lists the missing Hub runs and wrapped engraving or slot. The guide permits an air cut only.

Local results, after a clean trial merge with upstream/main `6732be131b3947ed09b088be7d662ee8c57d69ef`:

- The selected app test targets build. Ten suites pass, with 85 tests: continuous_4axis_part (7), first_4axis_part (4), fourth_axis_pose (9), index_swing (13), microarc_test_part (3), recorded_post_streams (5), rotary_feed_cap (11), tormach_fourth_axis (12), tormach_post (10), and tormach_wrapped_a (11).
- Three post suites pass, with 26 tests: explain_tormach (3), recorded_streams (12), and script_tormach (11).
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- All 13 affected site tests pass.
- Full site discovery reports three assertion failures and three errors. An archive of unchanged upstream main has the same failures and errors. The assertions concern the machine registry source and the missing tool-wire icon. The errors occur because Zola is not installed. I could not run `zola check`.
- The quick gate dry run completes. Its broad plan includes changes from main and shared fixtures. I ran the selected suites above.

Mutation checks:

- I used a temporary Cargo test harness outside the repository. It changes the CPS text in memory. It does not change repository code.
- Restore the old endpoint-distance calculation: RED in both units. The metric case samples 0.006861819340 mm in 0.017320516151 minutes. This exceeds the requested F0.1 mm/min.
- Restore strict text comparison: RED. The synthetic platform pair fails the bounded-comparison test.
- Disable both mutations: GREEN. All 13 harness tests pass.

Golden checks:

- I checked all 3,213 lines of the example and all 3,245 lines of the wrapped golden.
- Compared with the earlier reviewed head, 448 example lines and 529 golden lines change. Only F words and A rounding differ. Each A difference is at most 0.001 degree. Line counts, XYZ words and mode words stay the same.
- I sampled every turning feed at 256 intervals in the part frame. All 2,737 example turns and 2,678 golden turns hold the programmed feed and the 360 deg/min A limit. The largest sampled feeds are 203.168174 and 203.175370 mm/min, below 203.2 mm/min.
- All feed lines have positive F words. G94 is active before rapids, M5 and M30.
- The changed tilt refusal matches the recorded-stream test.

Requested before merge: none.

No PR change affects crates/ui. Before/after UI screenshots are not required. No restricted build script, workflow, scripts/ file, or dependency changes are present. No GitHub runner was used. No Hub or hardware run was done.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed the two findings from the latest review.

1. Refreshed this branch with upstream main. PR #2386 superseded #2342 and supplies the bounded relative F comparison. `wrap_golden_allows_only_bounded_platform_rounding` pins the reported Windows numeric pair. Restoring the old 0.04 allowance makes it RED. Restoring the fix makes it GREEN. All four `microarc_test_part` tests pass on Linux.

2. The inherited post restates G94 before a turning rapid. `g94_comes_back_before_a_turning_rapid_after_a_g93_feed` pins this behavior. Removing the restatement makes it RED. Restoring it makes it GREEN. All 13 `tormach_wrapped_a` tests pass, including independent trajectory and rate checks.

The merge preserves both guide explanations and the simulator disclaimer. No new screenshots or review evidence are committed.

Validation on Linux:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 548 steps, one failed. `continuous_4axis_part::the_continuous_4axis_part_posts_its_wrapped_program` fails at line 158 on the stale serialized project fixture. The other six continuous tests pass, including the loaded-project NC comparison.
- App/post clippy passes with all targets and `-D warnings`.
- The two affected site files have 25 passing tests and one failure. `test_machine_table_is_the_machine_file` expects the old A travel limits removed by main.

The remaining fixture and table failures are outside the latest review findings. They are unchanged. This run did not use Windows. The Windows review of #2386 records passing wrapped golden and turning-rapid checks: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2386#pullrequestreview-5949287713

New head: `6ae22ce1b4ebfa8eb7fa4dcda2224e4df4023497`.

Please re-review. The PR remains a draft. Existing labels are unchanged.

1. **[P2] Refresh the project fixture and make its construction test pass.** `crates/app/tests/continuous_4axis_part.rs:158` fails on the trial merge.    ```text

   ```text
   test result: FAILED. 6 passed; 1 failed
   ```

2. **[P3] Update the guide and its test for the current machine limits.** `site/content/guide/getting-started/first-continuous-4axis-part.md:74` says the shipped machine limits A to -360..360. The current machine file leaves that travel unstated. Lines 174-177 also say Rotary Offset is refused because of that limit. The same obsolete claim appears at `site/content/guide/multi-axis/continuous-4-axis.md:81`. Update these statements and the related chart captions and decision text. Distinguish any intentionally bounded example machine from the shipped machine. Update `site/tests/test_first_continuous_4axis_part.py:183`, which fails because it requires the removed travel field. The current `shipped_microarc_posts_wrapped_a_past_four_turns` test passes.

Local macOS results after a clean trial merge with upstream/main `f2d78f31127bd0851d1fefa88b5dc817f65aa19b`:

- The three selected app test targets build.
- `continuous_4axis_part`: 6 pass, 1 fails as described above. The loaded-project NC comparison and its sampled trajectory checks pass.
- `microarc_test_part`: all 4 pass.
- `tormach_wrapped_a`: all 13 pass, including the trajectory, platform-pair, continuous-turn, and turning-rapid coverage.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passes.
- The affected site suite: 12 pass, 1 fails as described above.

- The quick gate dry run completes. Its merge-base selection includes main changes and falls back to batch. I ran the selected suites above, not that full batch.

Mutation checks used temporary files outside the repository:

- Restore strict NC text comparison: RED. The platform-rounding acceptance test fails.
- Widen the permitted A difference from 0.001 to 0.002 degree: RED. The rejection test detects the wider allowance.
- Restore the original comparator: GREEN, both tests pass.

NC audit:

- I compared all 3,213 example lines with the earlier reviewed head `764df9f4ebf32b22a550bc816d9fd86a67cc42aa`. Every line is unchanged.
- I checked each line for finite numeric words, positive feeds, mode transitions, and A continuity. I sampled all 2,720 turning feeds at 256 intervals in the part frame.
- The largest sampled feed is 7.998747001 in/min, below the programmed 8 in/min. The largest A rate is 360 deg/min within floating-point precision. G94 is active before rapids, M5, and M30.

No crates/ui change requires screenshots. No restricted build-script, workflow, scripts/ file, or dependency change is present. Windows and Linux were not run here. No GitHub runner, Hub run, or machine run was used. No repository source or fixture was changed for this review.

The PR stays a draft. The existing `merge-ready` and `needs-rework` labels remain under the upstream disagreement rule. This review has blockers and does not clear NeoTech's held review state.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
